It is NOT a replacement authority. No FIBDB053_RUNTIME_COMPANION_EXECUTION_AUTHORITY_v1.0.1.json exists or is authorized. The parent remains controlling for every clause this amendment does not name.
BASE_AUTHORITY.why_no_parent_edit: The parent is a frozen artifact that has already been read by an independent certification refresh, and its defect is part of the evidentiary record that produced F-IC-1. Rewriting it would destroy the history of the defect and would be a prohibited historical-evidence rewrite (CLAUDE.md section 5). The defect is therefore adjudicated in place, in the open, by an append-only successor clause.
BASE_AUTHORITY.naming_derivation: Derived mechanically from repository precedent, not from the mission prompt. Every append-only authority correction in this repository is named <BASE_PACKAGE_ID>_AMENDMENT_v<next>.json and is placed in the SAME directory as its base, paired with a <BASE_MANIFEST_ID>_AMENDMENT_v<next>.json. The base is FIBDB053_RUNTIME_COMPANION_EXECUTION_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0 under docs/ops/wave3/, so this artifact is FIBDB053_RUNTIME_COMPANION_EXECUTION_AUTHORITY_AMENDMENT_v1.0.1.json under docs/ops/wave3/.

SECTION_A1_DEFECT_ADJUDICATION.SOURCE: Independent certification refresh of PR #189. That refresh independently confirmed that the compatibility contradiction still exists, that the runtime architecture is otherwise sound, that no ODS is required, and that the defect is internal to the authority/test contract rather than to the selected architecture.
SECTION_A1_DEFECT_ADJUDICATION.DEFECT_SUMMARY: The frozen parent asserts that the three textual spellings of the same PostgreSQL function signature are not interchangeable, and that a probe written in the wrong spelling is silently and permanently FALSE. That assertion is false. pg_catalog.to_regprocedure normalizes type aliases and discards type modifiers before performing an exact type-identity lookup, so all three spellings resolve to the SAME pg_proc OID. Because the mutation MUT-RC-12 consists of rewriting the literal in one of those interchangeable spellings, the mutant is INDISTINGUISHABLE from the original: N-RC-10 can never go RED for it. MUT-RC-12 and N-RC-10 are therefore VACUOUS as formulated - they name a mutation that does not mutate anything.

DEFECTIVE_CLAUSES.OLD_verbatim: The same signature has THREE spellings in this repository, and they are not interchangeable. A probe written in the wrong grapheme can be silently and permanently FALSE, which would pin the bridge to OLD_DB forever on a database that is already NEW_DB — a fail-silent inversion, not a fail-closed one.
DEFECTIVE_CLAUSES.defect: FALSE PREMISE. Both of its two claims are false. (a) "they are not interchangeable" - measured: all three resolve to one OID. (b) "A probe written in the wrong grapheme can be silently and permanently FALSE" - measured: a probe written in any of the three recorded graphemes is permanently TRUE on NEW_DB. The hazard it names does not exist in the form it names it.
DEFECTIVE_CLAUSES.disposition: SUPERSEDED by SECTION_A3 of this amendment.

DEFECTIVE_CLAUSES.OLD_verbatim: CATALOG_PROBE_CONTRACT.signature_graphemes. This mutant FAILS SILENT — the probe returns NULL forever and the bridge pins itself to OLD_DB on a NEW_DB database, filing no risk while reporting success.
DEFECTIVE_CLAUSES.defect: VACUOUS. It asserts the mutant "FAILS SILENT - the probe returns NULL forever". Measured: the mutant returns the SAME non-NULL OID as the canonical literal. The mutation is not merely hard to catch, it is not a mutation at all.
DEFECTIVE_CLAUSES.disposition: SUPERSEDED by SECTION_A4 of this amendment, together with the MUT-RC-12 mutation string it describes.

DEFECTIVE_CLAUSES.OLD_verbatim: Probe grapheme. The probe literal uses the to_regprocedure INPUT grapheme, not the pg_catalog grapheme (bpchar/varchar/int4/_text) and not the SQL declaration grapheme. A probe in the wrong grapheme returns NULL forever, pinning the bridge to OLD_DB on a database that is already NEW_DB — filing no risk while reporting success. This mutant FAILS SILENT, so a control asserting only 'the bridge works' passes it; the control must assert the probe returns TRUE against a real catalog holding the nine-argument function. Catches MUT-RC-12.
DEFECTIVE_CLAUSES.defect: VACUOUS AND SELF-DEFEATING. It instructs the control to assert that the probe returns TRUE against a real catalog holding the nine-argument function - which the pg_catalog-grapheme mutant ALSO satisfies. A control whose assertion is satisfied by its own declared mutant proves nothing about that mutant.
DEFECTIVE_CLAUSES.disposition: SUPERSEDED by SECTION_A5 of this amendment and re-expressed in the companion manifest amendment.

DEFECTIVE_CLAUSES.OLD_verbatim: Write the probe literal in the pg_catalog grapheme instead of the to_regprocedure input grapheme. Fails silent. Must be caught by N-RC-10.
DEFECTIVE_CLAUSES.defect: VACUOUS. Same false premise, restated in the manifest. "Fails silent" is measured to be "does not fail at all".
DEFECTIVE_CLAUSES.disposition: SUPERSEDED by SECTION_A4 of this amendment and re-expressed in the companion manifest amendment.

SECTION_A1_DEFECT_ADJUDICATION.THIS_AMENDMENT_DOES_NOT_PRETEND_THE_OLD_: BINDING. The parent clauses were false when written. This amendment records that they were false, records how that was measured, and replaces them. It does not reinterpret them charitably, does not describe the correction as a clarification, and does not claim the parent meant something other than what it says.
SECTION_A1_DEFECT_ADJUDICATION.WHAT_THE_PARENT_GOT_RIGHT_AND_THIS_AMEND: The parent chose to_regprocedure for a correct and measured reason (why_to_regprocedure: totality), imposed a FIXED LITERAL rule on the probe argument, named the to_regprocedure input form as the one the probe uses, and recorded the other two spellings as reader aids against db/hosted/authority/recovered-boundaries.ts and the Stage-A package. All four of those survive this amendment unchanged. The defect is confined to WHY a fixed literal is required, and to the mutation that was built on the wrong why.

SECTION_A2_REAL_PG_REPRODUCTION.disposition: MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED. Every row below was produced by executing the stated SQL against a real PostgreSQL catalog in a disposable container, which was destroyed afterwards.

OLD_DB_STATE.installed: uellix_stella_ops.complete_operation_ticket(character,uuid,character,character varying,character varying,integer,jsonb) - created as (char(64), uuid, char(64), varchar(100), varchar(100), integer, jsonb) and rendered by the catalog in exactly the predecessor form the parent authority records.
OLD_DB_STATE.verdict: OLD_DB. The canonical nine-argument literal resolves FALSE against a catalog holding only the seven-argument form, exactly as CATALOG_PROBE_CONTRACT.rule requires.

NEW_DB_STATE.transition: DROP FUNCTION ...(char(64), uuid, char(64), varchar(100), varchar(100), integer, jsonb); CREATE FUNCTION ...(char(64), uuid, char(64), varchar(100), varchar(100), integer, jsonb, varchar(50), text[]). This is the Stage-A shape: the seven-argument signature is dropped, not kept alongside.

GRAPHEME_MATRIX.literal: uellix_stella_ops.complete_operation_ticket(char(64), uuid, char(64), varchar(100), varchar(100), integer, jsonb, varchar(50), text[])

NEW_DB_STATE.GRAPHEME_MATRIX_VERDICT: ALL THREE RESOLVE TO THE SAME OID 16670. The parent clause "they are not interchangeable" is FALSE. to_regprocedure parses the signature, normalizes type aliases (character/bpchar, character varying/varchar, integer/int4, text[]/_text) and DISCARDS type modifiers (char(64) and character are the same type for signature identity), then performs an exact type-identity lookup. Spelling is therefore not a degree of freedom the probe can get wrong.

TOTALITY_MEASUREMENT.question: Can a wrong probe literal fail by raising, rather than by returning NULL?
inputs_tested: a literal naming a type that does not exist (nosuchtype at position 6)
the string "!!!not a signature at all!!!"
TOTALITY_MEASUREMENT.result: Every one returned NULL with psql exit code 0 and no SQLSTATE.
TOTALITY_MEASUREMENT.verdict: to_regprocedure is TOTAL over arbitrary input, not merely over absent functions. This is BROADER than the parent authority own why_to_regprocedure note, and it is load-bearing for this amendment in two ways. (a) It confirms that NO probe literal can ever fail by query error, so the distinction "fails for semantic signature mismatch rather than query error" is satisfied by every candidate mutant and is not a discriminator between them. (b) It is precisely why a dedicated control is genuinely required: the probe cannot self-detect its own typo, and nothing in the query layer will.

IMPLICIT_CAST_ASYMMETRY.question: Does to_regprocedure apply the implicit casts that ordinary function-call resolution applies?
measured: pg_cast holds integer -> bigint with castcontext = i (implicit).
An ordinary call resolves through it: with only castdemo(bigint) installed, SELECT castdemo(42::integer) succeeds and returns the bigint function result.
to_regprocedure of castdemo(bigint) resolves; to_regprocedure of castdemo(integer) returns NULL.
IMPLICIT_CAST_ASYMMETRY.verdict: to_regprocedure does EXACT type matching and does NOT apply implicit casts. This is the exact semantic OPPOSITE of the alias case: an alternate SPELLING of the same type resolves identically, while a DIFFERENT type that is implicitly castable does not resolve at all. That asymmetry is what the re-scoped MUT-RC-12 is built on, and it is the reason the re-scoped mutant is non-obvious enough to deserve a control.

SECTION_A2_REAL_PG_REPRODUCTION.CONCLUSION: F-IC-1 REPRODUCED. The parent signature_graphemes warning is false; MUT-RC-12 and N-RC-10 are vacuous in their v1.0.0 formulation.

SECTION_A3_SUPERSEDING_CATALOG_PROBE_CLA.supersedes: CATALOG_PROBE_CONTRACT.signature_graphemes.warning of the frozen parent, and that clause only.
SECTION_A3_SUPERSEDING_CATALOG_PROBE_CLA.NEW_warning: The same signature has THREE spellings in this repository and they ARE interchangeable for the probe: measured on a real PostgreSQL 17.6 catalog, all three resolve to the SAME pg_proc OID, because pg_catalog.to_regprocedure normalizes type aliases and discards type modifiers before an exact type-identity lookup. The three forms are recorded so that a reader comparing this contract against db/hosted/authority/recovered-boundaries.ts (pg_catalog form) or against the Stage-A package (SQL declaration form) does not mistake a spelling difference for a signature difference. The real hazard is NOT spelling. It is SEMANTIC SIGNATURE IDENTITY: a literal naming a different type, a different argument order, a different arity or a different function name resolves to NULL, and because to_regprocedure is total over arbitrary input it does so without raising - so a wrong signature is silently indistinguishable, at the query layer, from a function that is legitimately absent.

RETAINED_UNCHANGED_AND_STILL_BINDING.literal_rule: The probe argument is a FIXED LITERAL string. It is never composed, never interpolated, and never built from a variable holding a type name. The nine-argument signature is a constant of this contract.
RETAINED_UNCHANGED_AND_STILL_BINDING.literal_rule_disposition: NOT WEAKENED. The production probe MUST use ONE fixed, canonical literal. This amendment corrects only the JUSTIFICATION: the reason is not that a rival spelling would resolve differently (it would not), but that a fixed literal is the only form that is auditable against the Stage-A declaration, cannot be composed from a variable holding a type name, and gives N-RC-10 a single frozen comparand to assert against.
RETAINED_UNCHANGED_AND_STILL_BINDING.which_one_the_probe_uses: to_regprocedure_input_form. The other two are recorded so that a reader comparing this contract against db/hosted/authority/recovered-boundaries.ts (pg_catalog form) or against the Stage-A package (SQL declaration form) does not mistake a spelling difference for a signature difference.
RETAINED_UNCHANGED_AND_STILL_BINDING.three_recorded_graphemes_disposition: RETAINED verbatim as reader aids. Their recorded VALUES were never in error; only the warning attached to them was.

CANONICAL_PROBE_LITERAL.status: FROZEN BY THIS AMENDMENT. This exact string is the single canonical fixed literal the production probe uses.
required_resolution: Against NEW_DB (the nine-argument signature installed): to_regprocedure(<canonical literal>) IS NOT NULL must be TRUE.
Against OLD_DB (only the seven-argument signature installed): to_regprocedure(<canonical literal>) IS NOT NULL must be FALSE.
CANONICAL_PROBE_LITERAL.correctness_criterion: Correctness is about SEMANTIC SIGNATURE IDENTITY - schema, function name, argument arity, argument order and argument type identity - and NOT about textual alias spelling.

SECTION_A4_SUPERSEDING_MUT_RC_12.supersedes: MUTATION_CONTROLS.controls[MUT-RC-12].mutation and .guarantee_broken of the frozen parent, and the companion manifest mutation_controls[MUT-RC-12].description.
SECTION_A4_SUPERSEDING_MUT_RC_12.NEW_mutation: Change the SIXTH argument type of the probe literal from integer to bigint, leaving the schema, the function name, the argument order, the arity and every other argument type byte-unchanged.
SECTION_A4_SUPERSEDING_MUT_RC_12.NEW_guarantee_broken: CATALOG_PROBE_CONTRACT as amended by SECTION_A3: the probe literal must name the signature by SEMANTIC IDENTITY. This mutant FAILS SILENT in the only sense that is measurable - pg_catalog.to_regprocedure returns NULL with no SQLSTATE and psql exit code 0, so the probe query itself reports nothing wrong. The bridge then pins itself to OLD_DB on a database that is already NEW_DB.

WHY_THIS_MUTANT_AND_NOT_ANOTHER.smallest: It is a ONE-TOKEN substitution. No argument is added, removed or moved, and no other token changes. Among the seven candidates measured (wrong type at position 6, wrong type at position 7, swapped argument order, eight-argument arity, wrong function name, the predecessor seven-argument literal, and text in place of character varying at position 8) every one resolved NULL, so all were equally CAPABLE of failing the control; this one is the smallest.
WHY_THIS_MUTANT_AND_NOT_ANOTHER.genuinely_wrong_not_an_alias: integer (int4) and bigint (int8) are DIFFERENT TYPES with different OIDs, not two spellings of one type. This is exactly the distinction the parent authority got backwards.
WHY_THIS_MUTANT_AND_NOT_ANOTHER.non_obvious_and_therefore_worth_a_contro: integer -> bigint is an IMPLICIT cast in PostgreSQL (pg_cast castcontext = i), and ordinary function-call resolution DOES apply it - measured in SECTION_A2. A reader who knows that, and who also knows that character and bpchar resolve identically, could reasonably expect to_regprocedure to resolve the bigint spelling too. Measured, it does not. The mutant therefore tests a real belief a real implementer could hold, rather than an obvious typo.
WHY_THIS_MUTANT_AND_NOT_ANOTHER.syntactically_valid: MEASURED: the mutant literal is accepted by to_regprocedure, returns NULL, raises no SQLSTATE and leaves psql exit code 0. It fails for semantic signature mismatch, not for query error. Per SECTION_A2.TOTALITY_MEASUREMENT this is true of every possible probe literal, which is why the control cannot lean on an error to catch it.
WHY_THIS_MUTANT_AND_NOT_ANOTHER.deterministic: to_regprocedure performs exact type-identity matching with no cast application, so this mutant resolves NULL on every catalog whose installed sixth argument type is integer. It is not timing-, ordering- or role-dependent.
WHY_THIS_MUTANT_AND_NOT_ANOTHER.not_an_alternate_alias: EXPLICIT. This amendment forbids re-expressing MUT-RC-12 as any alternate spelling of the SAME type. The three recorded graphemes, and any other alias pair, resolve identically and would reinstate the vacuity this amendment exists to remove.

SECTION_A5_SUPERSEDING_N_RC_10.supersedes: The companion manifest negative_controls[N-RC-10].description of the frozen parent manifest, and that control only.
SECTION_A5_SUPERSEDING_N_RC_10.PROOF_OBLIGATION: N-RC-10 must prove, against ONE real PostgreSQL catalog in the NEW_DB state (the nine-argument signature installed and the seven-argument signature dropped), all three arms below. A naked "the probe works" assertion is INVALID.

ARMS.assertion: to_regprocedure(<canonical literal>) IS NOT NULL is TRUE.
ARMS.purpose: The canonical literal resolves. Without this arm the mutant arm could pass on a catalog where nothing resolves.

ARMS.assertion: to_regprocedure(<MUT-RC-12 mutant literal, sixth argument bigint>) IS NOT NULL is FALSE.
ARMS.purpose: The load-bearing arm. A and B taken together in the SAME catalog state are what make MUT-RC-12 a real mutation: the only difference between the two literals is the mutated token, so a divergence in the verdict can only be attributed to it.

ARMS.assertion: to_regprocedure(<pg_catalog grapheme>) resolves to the SAME OID as to_regprocedure(<canonical literal>).
ARMS.purpose: VACUITY GUARD. It pins the measured fact that alternate spellings are interchangeable, so a future lane cannot reintroduce the withdrawn grapheme mutation as if it were load-bearing. This arm goes RED only if a future PostgreSQL stops normalizing aliases, which would itself be a finding.

SECTION_A5_SUPERSEDING_N_RC_10.ANTI_VACUITY_RULE: N-RC-10 must assert the mutant literal as a FROZEN STRING, not by re-deriving it from the canonical literal with the same substitution the implementation uses. A control that re-expresses its subject own transformation proves only that the copy behaves like the copy.
SECTION_A5_SUPERSEDING_N_RC_10.substrate: Real PostgreSQL via pnpm db:audit:disposable against a fresh throwaway container, destroyed afterwards. Never a mock: the whole question is what a real catalog returns.

SECTION_A6_R1_ANCHOR_CORRECTION.scope: NON-SEMANTIC. This section corrects a cross-reference PATH and nothing else. No rollback behaviour, order, state or prohibition changes.

Per WAVE3_AUTHORITY's ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.interaction_with_stella_0017_rollback, running stella_0017_rollback.sql is NOT a valid reversal once 0017b is installed. This authority does not author that rollback; it records that the bridge's return path depends on it existing and being correct.

Measured at that file blob 1f78f175694cf0f89d976caa02931ea52dd4f06d: there is NO top-level ROLLBACK_CONTRACT key. The key exists at FIBDB053_STAGE_A_CONTRACT.ROLLBACK_CONTRACT.interaction_with_stella_0017_rollback.
SECTION_A6_R1_ANCHOR_CORRECTION.CITED_TEXT_AT_THE_CORRECTED_ANCHOR: stella_0017_rollback.sql restores the five-argument settle as a SELF-CONTAINED body and drops the ten-argument function. After stella_0017b is installed, running stella_0017_rollback.sql is therefore NOT a valid reversal path — it would drop a function stella_0017b's forward unit replaced with a wider one. This is exactly what the mandatory supersession entry exists to refuse. Recorded so an operator is not left to discover it at apply time.
SECTION_A6_R1_ANCHOR_CORRECTION.semantic_effect: NONE. The cited clause says exactly what R-1 says it says: running stella_0017_rollback.sql is not a valid reversal once 0017b is installed. R-1 dependency on stella_0017b_rollback.sql, its SUPPORTED state, its behaviour, its note, the required_order and the controls T7 and MUT-RC-10 are all unchanged.
SECTION_A6_R1_ANCHOR_CORRECTION.why_included_here: The refresh audit raised this alongside F-IC-1 and it is expressible append-only, as a pure path correction, without touching rollback semantics. It is recorded in this amendment rather than deferred so that a reader chasing the citation lands on the clause rather than on a key that does not exist. Had it required any change to rollback behaviour it would have been left to a separate amendment act.

SECTION_A7_BOUNDED_ONCE_COVERAGE.finding: The refresh audit found that CATALOG_PROBE_CONTRACT.invalidation_and_reprobe.bounded_once_rule is a binding runtime rule with NO manifest control proving its cardinality. Re-derived here: of the parent manifest 31 controls, none asserts how many times the probe is re-run. T5 is about idempotent replay and T7 is about probe inversion after rollback; neither counts probe invocations. The rule was therefore unfalsifiable.
SECTION_A7_BOUNDED_ONCE_COVERAGE.runtime_semantics_changed: NONE. The rule below is quoted from the frozen parent and is NOT altered by this amendment. Only its falsifiability changes.
SECTION_A7_BOUNDED_ONCE_COVERAGE.bounded_once_rule_verbatim: Exactly one re-probe and at most one retry. There is no loop, no backoff ladder and no second invalidation. An unbounded re-probe turns a deterministic contract into a retry storm against the catalog during precisely the window when the database is being changed.
SECTION_A7_BOUNDED_ONCE_COVERAGE.coverage_added: The companion manifest amendment adds negative control N-RC-11 (cardinality) and mutation control MUT-RC-13 (three mutants: a second re-probe, a retry loop, a backoff ladder). N-RC-11 must go RED for each.
SECTION_A7_BOUNDED_ONCE_COVERAGE.governance_check: PERMITTED, not forced. Verified against the frozen surfaces rather than assumed. (a) The parent manifest carries no self-check and pins no control count, so adding ids breaks no frozen count. (b) The parent AUTHORITY self_check pins MUTATION_CONTROLS.controls.length == 12 for ITS OWN section; this amendment adds NO authority-level mutation control, so that count remains true of the untouched v1.0.0 file. (c) The parent authority self-check "every MUTATION_CONTROLS entry names a must_be_caught_by that appears in the companion manifest" is one-directional authority-to-manifest and is unaffected by a manifest-only addition. (d) Repository precedent permits it: docs/ops/staging/CURRENT_SCHEMA_RUNTIME_ACL_SUCCESSOR_TEST_MANIFEST_AMENDMENT_v1.0.1.json introduced new control ids into an amendment manifest while its base kept its own counts. No separate amendment act is required, so BOUNDED_ONCE_COVERAGE does not remain open.

Next free negative id = N-RC-11; next free mutation id = MUT-RC-13; next free T id = T10, used for this amendment positive control. Intersection with the parent 31 ids is the EMPTY SET.
